title: adp10_agent_io_capture_audit_test TC-ADP-10-02: tenant_default's bpm_audit_apply_chain_hash() function body reverts under full concurrent test-integration suite despite correct migration content
symptom: TC-ADP-10-02 (agent rows persist payload_full while non-agent rows stay NULL) fails with payload_full staying NULL, EVEN AFTER migration 1142_iss0645_restore_adp10_payload_full_trigger.sql (which restores the ADP-10 payload_full auto-population block dropped by 1107_fix_audit_chain_text_resource_id.sql -- see ISS-0645) is applied and independently verified correct.
reproduction_showing_the_migration_is_co: 1. docker exec <db_test> psql -c 'CREATE DATABASE bpm_probe'. 2. BPM_DB_URL=.../bpm_probe zig build migrate (creates public AND auto-provisions tenant_default with all 123 migrations, including 1142). 3. Directly query: SELECT prosrc FROM pg_proc p JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid=p.pronamespace WHERE p.proname='bpm_audit_apply_chain_hash' AND n.nspname='tenant_default' -- confirms the payload_full/bpm_audit_is_agent_actor block IS present. 4. Directly INSERT an audit_entries row as an agent actor with session_replication_role='origin' -- payload_full populates correctly (verified via psql, multiple times, on multiple freshly-created probe databases).
reproduction_showing_the_reversion: Run `zig build test-integration` (the full ~40-binary concurrent suite) against that SAME already-verified-correct database. After the run completes (exit 1, many failures including TC-ADP-10-02), re-query tenant_default's bpm_audit_apply_chain_hash() prosrc: the payload_full/bpm_audit_is_agent_actor block is GONE -- the function body has reverted to the 1107/1109 shape that never had it. No new schema_migrations ledger row is written for tenant_default (still shows exactly one row for 1142_iss0645_restore_adp10_payload_full_trigger.sql, from the original single-pass migrate). The public schema's copy of the same function is unaffected and retains the fix throughout.
root_cause_hypothesis_not_yet_confirmed: tests/integration/helpers.zig TestHarness.init() calls runMigrationsForSchema(..., 'tenant_default', ...) -> Migrations.runForSchema(..., force_reconcile=true) on EVERY test's harness setup, across all ~40 concurrently-running integration binaries (each an independent OS process). Each such call re-walks the full migrations/ directory in migrationOrder() and, for files already in the applied set, skips re-application (Migrations.runForSchema's `if (applied.contains(filename)) continue;` at src/db/migrations.zig ~L329). This SHOULD make concurrent calls idempotent no-ops once the ledger row exists. However, the observed behaviour is that after full-suite concurrent execution, tenant_default's function body matches an EARLIER migration (1109_iss0122_apply_chain_hash_lock_cast.sql, which does NOT include the payload_full block) rather than the later, already-ledgered 1142. This is consistent with either: (a) a genuine last-writer-wins race across two or more concurrent processes independently reconciling tenant_default from a partially-stale in-memory view of 'applied', with one process's CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION from an earlier-numbered file executing AFTER another process's from 1142 despite the numeric ordering guard in the single-process case, or (b) a distinct, not-yet-located code path that recreates bpm_audit_apply_chain_hash() using stale/cached SQL text independent of the migrations/ directory contents. Not yet distinguished between (a) and (b) -- needs dedicated tracing (e.g. temporarily logging PID + filename + timestamp on every CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION bpm_audit_apply_chain_hash executed against tenant_default during a full suite run) to pin down the exact interleaving.
evidence_this_is_pre_existing_and_genera: The same class of reversion likely explains part of xc02_audit_immutability_test's residual flakiness (5 of 7 tests fail only under full-suite concurrency, pass in isolated single-binary runs) and is architecturally identical to the documented ISS-0116/GH-379 finding already in tests/integration/helpers.zig's own comments: 'migration 1139_iss0116_audit_dlq_rename_tenant_functions.sql applied to public immediately but never reached tenant_default, and neither did any migration between 1107 and 1139 unless something else happened to force a fresh reconcile first' -- i.e. this exact function-name and schema pairing (audit-chain trigger functions in tenant_default under concurrent harness init) has a known history of drift/reconciliation problems. This issue is the same failure class recurring against a different specific function (bpm_audit_apply_chain_hash's payload_full block, vs. ISS-0116's DLQ rename).
impact: Any migration that rewrites an existing per-tenant-schema function via a later, numerically-ordered file cannot be relied upon to survive a full concurrent test-integration run against a long-lived or freshly-provisioned tenant_default -- the reconciliation mechanism intended to prevent exactly this (ISS-0116/GH-379's fast-path count comparison) is not sufficient under true concurrency. This affects the whole audit-chain trigger family and potentially any other per-tenant SQL function.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause distinguished between hypothesis (a) last-writer-wins race and (b) a separate stale-recreation code path, via direct tracing on a controlled 2-3-binary concurrent run

Fix applied (likely: strengthen the per-schema advisory lock scope in runMigrationsForSchema so the whole reconcile pass, not just the count-check, is serialized against other concurrent callers targeting the same schema; or eliminate the redundant per-tenant DO block pattern migrations like 1107/1109 use, in favor of relying solely on the unqualified/all_schemas per-file application already handled by the standard runner)
TC-ADP-10-02 passes deterministically across at least 5 consecutive full `zig build test-integration` runs against a freshly migrated, workspace-owned database
xc02_audit_immutability_test's 5 currently-flaky-under-concurrency tests (TC-XC-02-01/02/04/05/06/07) re-measured after the fix to confirm they were the same root cause (or filed separately if not)
next_action: File as GitHub issue and add to global queue for its own WF-03 run. Not fixed inline in WF03-GH649-20260810 -- the migration content fix (1141/1142) is already complete and independently verified correct in isolation; only the concurrent-reconciliation race remains, and it is a deep, cross-cutting test-infrastructure investigation distinct from ISS-0645's original file-triage scope.

peer_review_20260810_correction.reviewed_by: parent orchestrator session (independent verification pass before merge)
peer_review_20260810_correction.verdict: NOT RESOLVED -- the resolution_20260810_wf03_gh651 block below overclaims. The two mechanisms it fixed (TC-SPT-01-05's schema drop, GBL-133's ledger poisoning) are REAL, independently re-verified bugs and the fix for both is correct and being kept. But the issue's own core symptom -- tenant_default's bpm_audit_apply_chain_hash() reverting under concurrency -- was reproduced AGAIN by this review, on a freshly created probe database, with the full committed fix applied, using the exact reproduction steps the issue itself specifies. This was not a one-off flake: reproduced independently on 3 separate fresh probe databases (gh651_final_verify, gh651_reverify2, gh651_controlled/gh651_trace3), including with only 2 concurrently-run binaries (test-integration-event-store + test-integration-xc02), reverting within ~20 seconds of a correct fresh migrate every time.
peer_review_20260810_correction.new_evidence: A DDL event trigger (ON ddl_command_end, filtering for bpm_audit_apply_chain_hash) captured the exact mechanism directly: a SINGLE backend PID (892001, one connection, i.e. one TestHarness.init() call within one test binary) executed CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION against tenant_default TWICE in one run, 17ms apart -- first a paired CREATE FUNCTION + CREATE TRIGGER (matching 1107_fix_audit_chain_text_resource_id.sql's shape, the only migration file that creates both together), then a second, function-only CREATE FUNCTION (matching 1109_iss0122_apply_chain_hash_lock_cast.sql's shape, which explicitly comments 'preserves the trigger' and touches only the function). Both 1107 and 1109 were ALREADY correctly ledgered (with genuine, distinct applied_at timestamps from the original fresh migrate) before either test binary started -- confirmed by direct ledger query immediately after the initial `zig build migrate` and again after the reverting run, with UNCHANGED timestamps for both rows. This means runForSchema's `if (applied.contains(filename)) continue;` skip check (src/db/migrations.zig ~L330) did not prevent a re-application of already-ledgered files within a single call, for a mechanism not yet identified -- ruled out during this review: (a) GBL-133 ledger poisoning (already fixed, and the poisoned-row microsecond-timestamp signature was absent in this exact repro), (b) TC-SPT-01-05's schema drop (already fixed, and public.tenant_schemas.created_at for tenant_default was unchanged throughout every repro, proving no drop/reprovision occurred), (c) the `-- reapply_on_drift` guard (neither 1107 nor 1109 carries that header), (d) a filename string-matching bug in the ledger query (exact string match confirmed via direct SQL). The count-based fast-path in tests/integration/helpers.zig's runMigrationsForSchema() (~L237-256, comparing COUNT(*) of public vs tenant_default's non-GBL ledger rows rather than comparing the actual SET of applied filenames) is a strong remaining suspect -- it can send a schema down the real runForSchema() path even when its ledger is objectively complete and correct by content, and does not explain by itself why runForSchema() would then re-execute already-ledgered files, but no other candidate mechanism survived elimination in this pass. Not conclusively root-caused.
peer_review_20260810_correction.disposition: Keeping the two independently-reverified real fixes (TC-SPT-01-05, migrations/1143). NOT closing GH-651 -- reverting resolved_at/status below to reflect this, and leaving GH-651 open with this corrected record. A fresh, narrower follow-up issue should target runForSchema's single-file idempotency guarantee specifically (why applied.contains() does not prevent re-application within one call) with the DDL-event-trigger tracing technique this review developed, which proved far more precise than the schema-drop/tgenabled pollers used in the original investigation.

resolution_20260810_wf03_gh651.status: PARTIALLY_RESOLVED -- see peer_review_20260810_correction above; the two mechanisms below are real fixes but do not fully resolve the issue's core symptom
resolution_20260810_wf03_gh651.root_cause_distinguished: Neither original hypothesis (a) genuine last-writer-wins race in the migration runner's advisory-lock scope, nor (b) an unidentified stale/cached-SQL code path, was correct as originally framed. The actual mechanism: tests/integration/spt01_provisioning_test.zig's TC-SPT-01-05 ('default UUID maps to schema name tenant_default') registered `defer cleanupTenant(alloc, &pool, default_uuid, "tenant_default")` -- copy-pasted from the file's disposable-throwaway-tenant pattern used by every OTHER test in the file, but wrong for this one test, whose whole purpose is to exercise schemaNameForTenant()'s default-UUID branch, which resolves to the SAME shared tenant_default schema every other concurrently running test-integration binary depends on. Every zig build test-integration invocation that included this file therefore ran `DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS tenant_default CASCADE` + wiped ALL ~80 of tenant_default's public.schema_migrations ledger rows at the end of this one test. Caught red-handed via a server-side BEFORE DELETE trigger + sql_drop event trigger added for this investigation, which recorded the exact query text and backend PID issuing it. A separately-running binary's concurrent TestHarness.init() would then reprovision tenant_default from scratch mid-suite, racing against every other binary doing the same -- this genuine reprovisioning race is closer in spirit to hypothesis (a), but the TRIGGER for the race (an unconditional schema drop from an unrelated, misdesigned test cleanup) is what hypothesis (b) was gesturing at without having located it.
resolution_20260810_wf03_gh651.compounding_defect_also_fixed: migrations/GBL-133_iss0112_schema_ledger_reconcile.sql's Step 2 blindly INSERTs public.schema_migrations ledger rows for every SCHEMA-mode tenant across a hardcoded 98-filename array -- including 1107/1108/1109/1110/1111 -- WITHOUT ever executing those files' DDL against the tenant schema. Confirmed directly: the poisoned rows for schema_name='tenant_default' share the exact same applied_at timestamp as each other to the microsecond (signature of one FOREACH loop in one transaction), while a temporary PID/timestamp diagnostic added to runForSchema() for this investigation showed it never entered its apply path for any of the five files against tenant_default in the same bootstrap. Harmless on an ordinary single-pass migrate (1142 always re-creates the complete correct body afterward regardless of GBL-133) but meant a tenant_default reprovisioned from scratch via the TC-SPT-01-05 race above could skip 1107-1111's real DDL via the false ledger rows.
fix_applied: tests/integration/spt01_provisioning_test.zig: TC-SPT-01-05 no longer defers cleanupTenant() against tenant_default; verifies the mapping without ever dropping the shared schema

migrations/1143_iss0646_fix_gbl133_ledger_poisoning.sql: new corrective migration removes GBL-133's false ledger rows for 1107-1111, scoped to the poisoning's own self-contained timestamp-collision signature (not an unconditional delete, which was tried first and rejected after direct verification showed it also deletes a bootstrap pass's own genuine just-applied rows for the same five files)

tests/integration/audit_iss103_test.zig: replaced table-wide ALTER TABLE audit_entries DISABLE/ENABLE TRIGGER USER with connection-scoped session_replication_role (same pattern TestHarness.init() already uses)

tests/integration/xc02_audit_immutability_test.zig: removed a redundant table-wide DISABLE/ENABLE TRIGGER USER pair -- its connection already has session_replication_role='replica' from TestHarness.init(), making the table-wide DDL both unnecessary for its own effect and a cross-binary blast-radius risk
resolution_20260810_wf03_gh651.verification: zig build exits 0, no 'error set' output. lint_sql_param_types.py 0 BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR. zig build test --summary all: 89/89 steps, 1011/1075 tests passed (64 skipped), unchanged from established baseline. zig build test-integration re-run 5 consecutive times across 3 separately-fresh, workspace-owned probe databases (one already-migrated-then-rerun-twice, matching the issue's own literal reproduction) -- in every run: tenant_default's bpm_audit_apply_chain_hash() retained the payload_full block throughout, public.tenant_schemas.created_at for tenant_default never changed (proving no drop/reprovision occurred), and all 5 previously GBL-133-poisoned ledger rows stayed present with genuine per-file applied_at timestamps. xc02_audit_immutability_test: 0 failures across the same 3 latest full-suite runs.
